literal: guard the tree stump and wait for a rabbit
meaning_long: waiting for luck instead of working for it
source: 《韩非子·五蠹》 (public domain), retold in our own words.
cover: He waited all year\Nfor a FREE rabbit.
hook: He waited all year\Nfor a FREE rabbit.
story: Ancient China, the state of Song. A farmer is working in his field when a rabbit dashes past and runs straight into an old tree stump, knocking itself out. The farmer happily takes it home: what luck! The next day he throws down his hoe and sits by the stump, waiting for another rabbit. Day after day, no rabbit comes. His field fills with weeds, and the whole village laughs at him.
continuity: - THE FARMER: stocky man about 35, round face, short stubbly beard, a straw hat hanging on his back, patched ochre tunic, rolled-up brown trousers, a wooden hoe.
- THE RABBIT: a plump grey-brown wild rabbit with long ears; after it bumps into the stump it is only dazed, with little cartoon stars circling its head (comic, never hurt-looking, no blood).
- THE STUMP AND FIELD: one big old tree stump with a few roots at the edge of his small field; a little thatched farmhouse nearby.
- VILLAGER (only in I1 and I7): a cheerful old man with a long white beard, grey tunic and a basket on his back.
scenes: The twist (used as the hook, first frame of the video)

Autumn: the farmer sits on a tiny wooden stool right next to the tree stump, chin in his hands, staring at it hopefully, a cobweb on his straw hat; behind him his field is a jungle of tall weeds. On the path behind, the white-bearded villager laughs and points at him. Both faces clear. This is the most important image; the editor will push in on it.
Spring: the farmer works hard in his neat field, swinging his hoe, sweat drops flying, the old tree stump at the field's edge. (Only the farmer.)
A rabbit dashes across the field and runs head-first into the tree stump, little cartoon stars circling its dizzy head; in the background the farmer turns around in surprise, hoe in hand.
The farmer walks home grinning hugely, carrying the dazed rabbit in both arms like a prize. (Only the farmer and the rabbit.)
Next morning: the farmer tosses his hoe over his shoulder into the grass and sits down beside the stump, arms crossed, looking smug and very sure of himself. (Only the farmer.)
Sunset: the farmer sits by the stump yawning, bored, a few dry leaves falling around him, the field behind him starting to grow weeds; no rabbit anywhere. (Only the farmer.)
Wide shot: the farmer's field is completely overgrown with tall weeds; the farmer is a small figure sitting by the stump, while the white-bearded villager on the path laughs, holding his belly.
The stump (background for the big title)

The old tree stump with the farmer's wooden hoe leaning against it, covered in cobwebs, in the lower half of the frame. The upper half is a calm, plain sky with soft grey ink washes and almost nothing in it (we place the big title there). No people, no animals.

A modern living room: the same FARMER (round face, stubbly beard) in an ochre hoodie lies on the couch staring hopefully at a phone held up in front of him (screen facing away from the viewer), while a pile of untouched blank papers sits on the table and a cobweb hangs from the lamp. No other people. No text, no logos, no visible screens.
lines: He waited all year for a free rabbit.
This farmer worked hard in his field every day.
Suddenly, a rabbit ran straight into a tree stump!
He took it home. What luck!
The next day, he dropped his hoe and waited by the stump.
Day after day, no rabbit came.
His field filled with weeds, and everyone laughed.
Guard the stump, wait for a rabbit.
It means waiting for luck instead of working.
Like waiting to get lucky, instead of doing the work.
